texts.facts: This is an application/petition under Section 166 & 140 of Motor Vehicle Act filed by Sh. Subhash Chand Saroha (hereinafter called the petitioner) against Sh. Sushil Chauhan (hereinafter called the Respondent No.1), Jay Pee Ganga Infrastructure Corporation Ltd. (hereinafter called the Respondent No.2) and Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd. (hereinafter called the Respondent No.3) seeking compensation in respect of an accident which occurred on 01.05.2018 at about 8.30 a.m. near Kanavani Nahar, Ghaziabad, Up. Brief Facts 2. It is stated that claimant while riding on a motorcycle commuting from Swarn Jayantipuram to the Police Station Sector 14A, Noida got hit by a speeding Bolero bearing Registration No. UP32 CP 2651 (hereinafter called the offending vehicle) driven in a rash and negligent manner because of which he fell down and received serious injuries. It is stated that he rushed to Yashoda Hospital, Ghaziabad, where he remained admitted for five days and later continued his treatment as an Out Patient. FIR MACT No.901/2018 Subhash Chand vs. Sushil Page No. 2 of 28 was registered under Section 279/338/427 IPC. Upon completion of investigation, charge-sheet was filed against Respondent No.1 in the Court of Ld. CJM, Ghaziabad. 3. Notice of this petition was issued to all the respondents, in response to which, they appeared and filed their respective replies. REPLY 4. Respondent No.1 submitted in reply that the alleged offending vehicle was duly insured on the date of accident. It is also stated that he had a valid driving license. It is pointed in the said reply that the FIR was registered after a considerable delay. It is also submitted that the alleged offending vehicle was not involved in any accident. 5. Written Statement of Respondent No.2 also mentions about delay in registration of FIR with the contention that petitioner has twisted and fabricated the facts to get favourable order asserting that the offending vehicle is not involved in the accident which allegedly happened on 01.05.2018. 6. Written Statement on behalf of Respondent No. 3 mentions that the offending vehicle has been falsely implicated and has been planted for the purpose of grant of compensation. It is also pointed out that there is unreasonable and unjustifiable delay of 24 days in lodging the FIR which has not been explained. In the meanwhile, on 03.11.2022, applicant / claimant moved an application for assessment of disability which was called from concerned hospital. A Disability Certificate was received from Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya Hospital, New Delhi as noted in order dated 21.03.2023 wherein Medical Board opined that injured has suffered 47% permanent physical impairment in relation to his right lower limb. EVIDENCE : 9. On 30.03.2022, claimant examined himself as PW-1 and tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents i.e. copy of his Aadhar Card (Ex.PW1/1) and Original Medical documents and bills Ex.PW1/2 (colly), Certified copy of charge-sheet, Site Plan, Mechanical Inspection Report, Discharge Summary Ex.PW1/3 (colly). PW1 was cross- examined at length by Ld. Counsels for respective respondents. 10. During cross-examination on behalf of Respondent Nos. 1 and 2, PW1 described the mode and manner of accident. He categorically deposed that offending vehicle was coming from front on the wrong side and hit him because of which he fell MACT No.901/2018 Subhash Chand vs. Sushil Page No. 4 of 28 down. PW1 further deposed that he had clearly seen Registration Number of the offending vehicle after the accident. 11. During cross-examination on behalf of Respondent No.3 , PW1 deposed that on 01.05.2018 at the time of accident he was going on his motorcycle (make Honda Splender Pro Plus) to his office at Sector 14A, Noida, UP. PW1 further deposed that he was taken to hospital by public persons and that he had sent his son to lodge FIR immediately after the accident but police refused to lodge the same. He denied the suggestion that accident had taken place due to his own negligence as he was in drunken condition at the time of accident. He further denied that he has filed false and and fabricated bills. Subhash Chand vs Sushil Chauhan on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199694689/ 3 FINAL ARGUMENTS 12. Written submissions have also been filed by Ld. Counsel for Respondent No.3. 13. Ld. counsel for claimant contended that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle. He also stated that the delay in FIR was due to genuine medical reasons on the part of injured. Petitioner/PW-1 deposed on the lines of original complaint/ statement as recorded by IO during investigation on the basis of which charge-sheet was filed against driver of offending vehicle.
